summary: Nora can now work out that a short name and a long one are the same thing.
details: Exact matching already handled the easy cases — the same name in different capitalisation or spacing. What it cannot settle is an abbreviation against the full name, or two words that mean the same thing. Those now go to a background pass that decides them one at a time.

It can only ever add a name to something already known. It can never join two known things together: keeping two things apart is a mistake somebody can undo later, and joining two that were not the same absorbs everything said about both, which cannot be undone.
Being unsure is a complete answer and the expected one, and it is counted — so a pass that keeps deciding no is visible rather than looking like a pass that never ran.

The names it is offered are found by spelling similarity, which does not reach an abbreviation like HKO. That channel arrives with the vector search later; until then such a name is simply never offered, which costs a missed connection rather than a wrong one.
limitations: The prompt's reasoning and its worked examples are adapted from an open-source project under the Apache licence; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Whether it beats one written from scratch is untested, because there is no graded set of examples from this room to measure either against.
